title: A support fund for people new to the community
story: Most people who take shahadah at our centre never come back after the second month. Some are not on speaking terms with their families, some have moved out with a bag, and almost none of them know anyone. We are raising 25,000 GBP for a two-year support fund: a mentor for the first year, weekly classes, a shared meal every fortnight, and a small emergency grant for anyone who ends up with nowhere to sleep or nothing to eat. Last year we found 900 GBP for four people out of the general fund and it ran out in March.
reviewerNote: Information requested, after I put it to our advisor. The reconciled hearts line itself I have recorded as supported: the copy describes convert care in the terms the heading is glossed in, people who took shahadah and then had nobody, and there is no fact about that heading the page leaves out. What is unresolved is our own question and not theirs. Whether this category still operates at all is genuinely disputed between contemporary bodies, and one of them moved on it as recently as this year, so our policy does not let a badge rest on that question by itself. The question I put to the advisor was about our own policy rather than about the underlying difference, and the answer was to look for an independent basis in the campaign. So I have asked the organizer what share of the fund is emergency grants going to individuals, and whether those recipients are in material need at the point they receive it, since that would put part of this campaign somewhere I can assess on evidence. None of this is a finding against the organizer or against the category, and I said so in the message, because a request that reads as a soft refusal will not get me the facts I need.
